simple.meaning: תֻּכִּי (tukkîy) is a Hebrew word meaning “probably of foreign derivation; some imported creature , probably a peacock.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: תֻּכִּי (H8500) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 10:22, with occurrences in 1 Kings, 2 Chronicles.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תֻּכִּי (H8500) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in תֻּכִּי (H8500) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: תֻּכִּי (tukkîy) / H8500 is traced through 1 Kings 10:22, 2 Chronicles 9:21 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

occurrences.englishText: For the king had a fleet of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish came, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
For the king had ships that went to Tarshish with Huram’s servants. Once every three years, the ships of Tarshish came bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
